text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Mālatī**, one of Śrī Rādhā's maidservants — the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi names her among Śrī Rādhā's **prāṇa-sakhīs (and again among the priya-sakhīs)**.

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the sakhīs who love Śrī Rādhā more

> atha sakhī pañca-vidhā | sakhī, nitya-sakhī, prāṇa-sakhī, priya-sakhī, parama-preṣṭhā-sakhī | āsāṁ madhye kācit sama-snehā kācid asama-snehā | … yā rādhikāyāṁ snehādhikā sā nitya-sakhī |
> nitya-sakhyas tu kastūrī manojñā maṇi-mañjarī
> sindūrā candanavatī kaumudī madirādayaḥ (Sakhī-bheda, text 5)

- «There are five different types of sakhīs: (1) sakhī, (2) nitya-sakhī, (3) prāṇa-sakhī, (4) priya-sakhī and (5) parama-preṣṭha-sakhī. Of these, some possess equal affection for both Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa (sama-sneha), while others are partial to either Śrī Rādhā or Śrī Kṛṣṇa (viṣama-sneha).»

- «The most prominent nitya-sakhīs are known as prāṇa-sakhīs. Examples are Tulasī, Keli-kandalī, Kādambarī, Śaśimukhī, Candralekhā, Priyambadā, Madonmadā, Madhumatī, Vasantī, Kalabhāṣinī, Ratnāvalī, Mālatī and Karpūralatikā. All of these gopīs are equal in beauty to Vṛndāvaneśvarī Śrīmatī Rādhikā.»
- «Vraja damsels such as Mālatī, Candralatikā, Guṇachūḍā, Varāṅgadā, Mādhavī, Candrikā, Prema Mañjarī, Tanumadhyamā and Kandarpa-sundarī are ten million in number. They are all examples of priya-sakhīs» (pp. 23–25).

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the maidservants

- **Paricārikās**: among the messengers who bring Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa together, «Sakhīs such as **Lavaṅga Mañjarī and Bhānumatī Mañjarī** are called paricārikā, servants, or assistants… According to the necessity of the time, all sakhīs act as messengers» (Dūtī-bheda, text 4, p. 22). «A nisṛṣṭārthā-dūtī performs all services upon receiving a command and personally shoulders the total responsibility of arranging the meeting between Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa» (p. 21).
- **A maidservant of Rādhā** (introduction, pp. xiii–xiv): when envious scholars waited in a grove to kill Viśvanātha Cakravartī, «he suddenly disappeared, and in his place, a beautiful young girl of Vraja appeared, picking flowers with her friends… she replied, “I am a maidservant of my mistress, Śrīmatī Rādhikā. She is presently at Her in-laws' house at Yāvaṭa. She has sent me here to pick flowers.”»
- **Their mistress**: «Śrīmatī Rādhikā is His constitutional pleasure potency (svarūpa-bhūtā-hlādinī-śakti)… The other gopīs are Śrīmatī Rādhikā's direct and non-different expansions (kāya-vyūha), manifestations (prakāśa) or partial manifestations (aṁśa-svarūpa)» (pp. 3–4). «Although mohana-mahābhāva is awakened within all the sakhīs in Śrīmatī Rādhikā's yūtha (group), it is most awakened in Śrīmatī Rādhikā» (p. 43).
- **Her group's love**: «Śrīmatī Rādhikā and the gopīs who follow Her possess mañjiṣṭhā-rāga, which is independent, having no basis other than itself. It eternally increases and becomes more and more splendid» (p. 41); «Adhirūḍha-mahābhāva is seen only in Śrīmatī Rādhikā's group» (p. 46).

- **Paricārikās**: among the messengers who bring Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa together, «Sakhīs such as **Lavaṅga Mañjarī and Bhānumatī Mañjarī** are called paricārikā, servants, or assistants… According to the necessity of the time, all sakhīs act as messengers» (Dūtī-bheda, text 4, p. 22). «A nisṛṣṭārthā-dūtī performs all services upon receiving a command and personally shoulders the total responsibility of arranging the meeting between Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa» (p. 21).
- **A maidservant of Rādhā** (introduction, pp. xiii–xiv): when envious scholars waited in a grove to kill Viśvanātha Cakravartī, «he suddenly disappeared, and in his place, a beautiful young girl of Vraja appeared, picking flowers with her friends… she replied, “I am a maidservant of my mistress, Śrīmatī Rādhikā. She is presently at Her in-laws' house at Yāvaṭa. She has sent me here to pick flowers.”»
- **Their mistress**: «Śrīmatī Rādhikā is His constitutional pleasure potency (svarūpa-bhūtā-hlādinī-śakti)… The other gopīs are Śrīmatī Rādhikā's direct and non-different expansions (kāya-vyūha), manifestations (prakāśa) or partial manifestations (aṁśa-svarūpa)» (pp. 3–4). «Although mohana-mahābhāva is awakened within all the sakhīs in Śrīmatī Rādhikā's yūtha (group), it is most awakened in Śrīmatī Rādhikā» (p. 43).
- **Her group's love**: «Śrīmatī Rādhikā and the gopīs who follow Her possess mañjiṣṭhā-rāga, which is independent, having no basis other than itself. It eternally increases and becomes more and more splendid» (p. 41); «Adhirūḍha-mahābhāva is seen only in Śrīmatī Rādhikā's group» (p. 46).

## Sources

Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, pp. xiii–xiv, 3–4, Dūtī-bheda 4 (pp. 20–22), Sakhī-bheda 5 (pp. 23–25), Rati-bheda (pp. 41–43), Āśraya-nirṇaya 15 (p. 46).

## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Kalāvatī**, a gopī who sang the songs composed by Viśākhā.

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — Kalāvatī

The Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi names a **Kalāvatī** among the youngest gopīs (Vayo-bheda, p. 25–26): «The Vraja gopīs fall into four age groups: (1) vayaḥ-sandhi – the cusp of childhood and youth, (2) navya-yauvana – newly blossomed youth, (3) vyakta-yauvana – ripening youth and (4) pūrṇa-yauvana – fully blossomed youth. The juncture between paugaṇḍa (childhood) and yauvana (youth) is the stage known as vayaḥ-sandhi. It is also known as prathama-kaiśora, the first stage of adolescence. **Nāyikās such as Kalāvatī are situated in this stage of vayaḥ-sandhi.**» (It does not say if she is the Kalāvatī who sang Viśākhā's songs.)

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the sakhīs who love Śrī Rādhā more

> atha sakhī pañca-vidhā | sakhī, nitya-sakhī, prāṇa-sakhī, priya-sakhī, parama-preṣṭhā-sakhī | āsāṁ madhye kācit sama-snehā kācid asama-snehā | … yā rādhikāyāṁ snehādhikā sā nitya-sakhī |
> nitya-sakhyas tu kastūrī manojñā maṇi-mañjarī
> sindūrā candanavatī kaumudī madirādayaḥ (Sakhī-bheda, text 5)

- «There are five different types of sakhīs: (1) sakhī, (2) nitya-sakhī, (3) prāṇa-sakhī, (4) priya-sakhī and (5) parama-preṣṭha-sakhī. Of these, some possess equal affection for both Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa (sama-sneha), while others are partial to either Śrī Rādhā or Śrī Kṛṣṇa (viṣama-sneha).»
- «**Those sakhīs with more affection for Śrīmatī Rādhikā are called nitya-sakhīs.** They include Kasturī, Manojñā, Maṇi Mañjarī, Sindūrā, Candanavatī, Kaumudī and Madirā.»
- «The most prominent nitya-sakhīs are known as prāṇa-sakhīs. Examples are Tulasī, Keli-kandalī, Kādambarī, Śaśimukhī, Candralekhā, Priyambadā, Madonmadā, Madhumatī, Vasantī, Kalabhāṣinī, Ratnāvalī, Mālatī and Karpūralatikā. All of these gopīs are equal in beauty to Vṛndāvaneśvarī Śrīmatī Rādhikā.»
- «Vraja damsels such as Mālatī, Candralatikā, Guṇachūḍā, Varāṅgadā, Mādhavī, Candrikā, Prema Mañjarī, Tanumadhyamā and Kandarpa-sundarī are ten million in number. They are all examples of priya-sakhīs» (pp. 23–25).

name: Dāmodara Paṇḍit
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Śaibyā**, one of the eight principal heroines of Vraja, the chief sakhī of Candrāvalī with Padmā: right-wing and soft-spoken, dressed in scarlet. (The books do not say whether she is the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā's Śaibyā; the name is the same.)

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — Śaibyā

> candrāvalī dakṣiṇā mṛdvī nīla-vastrā | asyāḥ sakhī padmā dakṣiṇā prakharā | śaibyā dakṣiṇā mṛdvī | sarvā eva rakta-vastrāḥ (Nāyikā-svabhāva, text 3)

«Candrāvalī is dakṣiṇā and mṛdvī and wears blue. Her two chief sakhīs are Padmā and Śaibyā. Padmā is dakṣiṇā and prakharā, while **Śaibyā is dakṣiṇā and mṛdvī. Both of them dress in scarlet**» (p. 21). *Dakṣiṇā*: «behave with the hero in a straightforward manner… they become controlled by the hero's praises»; *mṛdvī*: «use very gentle language» (pp. 18–19).

## Gopāla-campū — Śaibyā

- **Candrāvalī's sakhī** (Pūrva-campū 15, verse 53): «From that day, Viśākhā, Lalitā and others became the sakhīs of Rādhā. Padmā, Śaibya and others became the sakhīs of Candrāvalī»; «Candrāvalī's sakhīs like Śaibya and Padmā» (17.42).
- **In the rāsa** (Pūrva-campū 25, verse 32): «One slender gopī took his chewed betel nut in her palms, which appeared like the vessel holding attraction for him.» — «Her name was Śaibyā. She was situated to his right.»
- Kṛṣṇa's letter from Mathurā (Uttara-campū 6, verse 13): «O Padmā! O Bhadrā! O Śaibyā! When your three forms, with distressed hearts, rolled about near the tamāla tree out of separation from me, I was there.»
- **One of the eight heroines** (Uttara-campū 31.51): «O Rādhā, Candrāvalī, Lalitā, Viśākhā, Bhadrā, Śyāmā, Padmā, Śaibya!» In separation, «Śaibyā is weeping» (36, verse 8).
- **In Dvārakā** (Uttara-campū 17, verse 53): «Śaibyā was Mitravindā.»

## Compared with the Gaṇoddeśa

The Gaṇoddeśa text of this record calls Śaibyā «hot-tempered»; the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa makes Śaibyā **mṛdvī**, soft-spoken (it is Padmā who is *prakharā*). Whisper's rule: the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa and the Gopāla-campū take precedence.

## Sources

Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, Nāyikā-svabhāva 3 (pp. 17–21); Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 15.53, 17.42, 25.32; Uttara 6.13, 17.53, 31.51, 36.8.

name: Śrī Śivānanda Sena
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

The gopīs **Vīrā** and **Dūtī**, the messengers who brought the gopīs to Kṛṣṇa. The Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi names **Vīrā** among Kṛṣṇa's three famous messengers in Vraja: «Vīrā is pragalbha-vacanā (a harsh speaker)».

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the messengers of Vraja

> atha dūtī dvi-vidhā, svayaṁ dūti āpta-dūtī ca | tatrāpta-dūtī ca trividhāḥ, amitārthā nisṛṣṭārthā patra-hāriṇī ca | … tāḥ śilpa-kāriṇī daivajñā liṅginī paricārikā dhātreyī vanadevī sakhī cety ādayaḥ | vraje vīrā vṛndā vaṁśī ca kṛṣṇasya dūtī-trayam | pragalbha-vacanā vīrā vṛndā ca priya-vādinī, sarva-kārya-sādhikā vaṁśī (Dūtī-bheda, text 4)

- «A dūtī is defined as a sakhī who takes a message from the heroine to the hero, or vice versa. Svayaṁ-dūtī is the heroine herself, when she indicates to the hero the location of the meeting place. An āpta-dūtī is a follower who conveys the message.»
- «An amitārthā-dūtī acts as a messenger, although a verbal message is not conveyed to her. She simply comprehends an indication. A nisṛṣṭārthā-dūtī performs all services upon receiving a command and personally shoulders the total responsibility of arranging the meeting between Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa. A patra-hāriṇī is a messenger who carries letters and removes obstructions in the meeting of the hero and heroine.»
- «These messengers are artisans (śilpakāriṇī), fortune tellers (daivajñā), ascetics (liṅginī), servants (paricārikā), nurses (dhātreyī), forest goddesses (vana-devī), girlfriends (sakhī) and others… Those messengers who, like Purṇamāsī, wear the cloth of renunciation are called liṅginī… Sakhīs such as Lavaṅga Mañjarī and Bhānumatī Mañjarī are called paricārikā… Vṛndā-devī, the presiding goddess of Vṛndāvana, is known as a vana-devī… According to the necessity of the time, all sakhīs act as messengers.»
- «In Vraja, Śrī Kṛṣṇa has three famous messengers: Vīrā, Vṛndā and Vaṁśī. Vīrā is pragalbha-vacanā (a harsh speaker), Vṛndā is priya-vādinī (one who speaks sweetly), and Vaṁśī, Śrī Kṛṣṇa's flute, is sarva-kārya-sādhikā (one who accomplishes everything)» (pp. 20–22).

## Sources

Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, Dūtī-bheda 4 (pp. 20–22).
